editorial: Picture a crowded hallway where every whisper is a soundtrack to teenage longing. You’ll notice the film’s self‑aware narrative pokes fun at the social hierarchies of high school while keeping the stakes real. The director’s choice to let the cafeteria become a stage for confession scenes gives you a fresh sense of immediacy. A few moments stretch a bit, dragging the narrative pace. If you crave a laugh‑packed drama that tackles envy without slipping into melodrama, this is your next binge.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of campus dramedies who enjoy sharp dialogue and relatable angst.
similarMovies: To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before
